Both work: marking something read drops it from the "Read later" view while it stays safely in "All" (the All count never dropped from 6). Now please **compare the two mark/unmark gestures** — identical except for that action:

**Alternative 1 — a quiet on/off toggle.** Open **http://maker:4001/?rl=toggle**. Every card has a small control: `☆ Add to read later` when off, `★ In read-later — turn off` when on. Click the **"Read later" tab** at the top (it shows how many are waiting), then on one card click **"★ In read-later — turn off."** It leaves the unread view immediately; switch to **"All bookmarks"** and confirm it's still there, just no longer marked.

**Alternative 2 — a verb button that changes by context.** Open **http://maker:4001/?rl=action**. Here the button reads **"✓ Mark as read"** on items in your read-later list, and **"☆ Save to read later"** on items that aren't. Go to the **"Read later" tab**, click **"✓ Mark as read"** on one — it leaves the list. Then go to **"All bookmarks"** and click **"☆ Save to read later"** on something to see it get added (the tab count goes up).

A few things to react to:

- **Which gesture feels right** — the quiet always-there toggle, or the explicit "Mark as read" / "Save to read later" verb button? Or a blend?
- **The view switch itself:** I used two tabs — **"All bookmarks"** and **"Read later"** — with counts. Does that match your idea of a "separate view," and is "Read later" the right label (vs. "Unread," "To read," etc.)?
- **When your read-later list is empty**, I show an encouraging "You're all caught up 🎉" message. Does that feel right, or too cute?

Try both and tell me your preference — then read-later is the last piece needed to cover your whole goal.
